tasks.task: e2e suite stabilisation — route warm-up pass, and review specs that override the config timeout downward (c1 sets `page.setDefaultTimeout(15_000)`)
tasks.notes: Opened by Day 22, the first CI run. NOT a state bug — `verify-day-c1` failed on CI run 1 and PASSED on run 2 with NO fix applied (only the webhook secret changed), and five escalating local repros against a virgin DB could not reproduce it: alone, after day-19, with .env.local removed, on a cold .next, and in the full 65-spec run. A state bug fails identically; a timing flake does not. KNOWN-FLAKY SET — six specs, all timeouts on navigation/visibility, none an assertion that data was wrong: verify-day-c1, verify-day-c2, verify-day-19 (operator impersonation), verify-day-5, verify-day-6, verify-day-16 (accessibility). verify-day-c2 added from the Day 22 post-merge run on main (run 34126383303): 'a dealer detail page renders its state as a full name' flaked on the row-click navigation — toHaveURL(/dealers/<id>) timed out at 15 s (19× on http://localhost:3000/dealers), passed on retry — same signature. The faithful local repro run scored 61 passed / 3 flaky / 1 failed in 19.1m vs CI 19.4m, so the environments perform comparably and the instability is in the suite, not the runner. TWO PARTS: (1) a route warm-up pass so first-hit dev-server compilation (5–10 s/route, DEV.87) is not competing with test execution; (2) audit specs that TIGHTEN timeouts below the config — c1 sets page.setDefaultTimeout(15_000) against a 60 s config default while walking the heaviest cold-route path in the suite (/admin/tenants/new, /admin/tenants/[id], /change-password, three logins), and its own runtime doubled 14.2 s standalone → 28.7 s at the end of the full run. Sequenced BEFORE the Typst migration: F.38 rewrites the PDF specs and should land on a stable suite. DEV.93. DEV.101 — CI run 34223278188 (PR #3) went red on `e2e` with `"unexpected": 0`: NO test failed. Two known-flake retries (verify-day-19 38.6 s, verify-day-c1 36.9 s) burned 75.5 s, and the suite's own test time was 19.0 min of the 20.0 min `globalTimeout`, so the cap fired mid-run and 2 verify-day-c2 tests never ran. Recent green runs sit at 16m25s–19m10s against that 20 min cap and `main` itself passes at 18.2 min WITH 2 flakies — so two retries can now redden any branch including `main`. Both failures were 15 s navigation timeouts, and `verify-day-c1` sets `page.setDefaultTimeout(15_000)` against a 60 s config default. OPEN FOR THE OPERATOR, not decided: (a) whether "restore headroom against `globalTimeout`" becomes an explicit acceptance criterion here, and (b) whether the 20 min cap is still right — it was sized in DEV.81 to kill a Windows teardown hang, not to bound suite runtime.
